Lists Notion databases accessible by the: Lists Notion databases accessible by the connected account with pagination support.
Add a new item to a Notion database with: Ajouter un nouvel élément à une base de données Notion avec des valeurs de champs personnalisés et du contenu optionnel. Idéal pour créer des tâches, des enregistrements ou des entrées dans des bases de données structurées.
Update specific fields in a Notion datab: Mettre à jour des champs spécifiques dans une base de données Notion. Parfait pour maintenir les données, le suivi des modifications ou la synchronisation des informations entre les systèmes.
Searches for an item in database by fiel: Recherche un élément dans la base de données par champ.
Lists pages in a Notion database with op: Lists pages in a Notion database with optional field filters and pagination.
Create a new Notion page as a sub-page w: Créez une nouvelle page Notion en tant que sous-page avec un titre et un contenu personnalisés. Idéal pour organiser la documentation, les notes ou créer des hiérarchies structurées de pages.
Ajoute du contenu à la fin d'une page.
Retrieve the actual content of a page (r: Récupère le contenu réel d'une page (représenté par des blocs).
Archive (soft-delete) a database item wi: Archive (soft-delete) un élément de la base de données sans le supprimer définitivement. Les éléments archivés peuvent être restaurés plus tard si nécessaire.
Restore an archived database item back t: Restaurer un élément de base de données archivé à l'état actif. Parfait pour récupérer des tâches, des projets ou des enregistrements archivés accidentellement.
Add a comment to any Notion page to star: Ajoutez un commentaire à n'importe quelle page Notion pour commencer les discussions, fournir des commentaires ou laisser des notes pour la collaboration de l'équipe.
Get detailed information about a Notion: Obtenir des informations détaillées sur une base de données Notion incluant toutes ses propriétés, types de champs et configuration. Idéal pour construire des formulaires dynamiques, des règles de validation ou pour comprendre les schémas de base de données.
Retrieve all comments from a Notion page: Récupérez tous les commentaires d'une page Notion, organisée par fil de discussion. Parfait pour suivre les commentaires, gérer les commentaires ou surveiller les discussions de pages.
Search for Notion pages by title with fl: Rechercher des pages de notion par titre avec des options de correspondance flexibles. Idéal pour trouver des pages spécifiques, créer des références de pages ou créer des flux de travail automatisés basés sur la découverte de pages.
Creates a new sub-page under an existing: Creates a new sub-page under an existing Notion page, with a title and optional markdown body.
Fetches a single page's metadata and pro: Fetches a single page's metadata and property values by id (a database row is a page).
Archives (trashes) or restores any page: Archives (trashes) or restores any page or database row by id via its archived flag.
Moves a page under a different parent pa: Moves a page under a different parent page (or into a database as a row).
Appends new block content (parsed from m: Appends new block content (parsed from markdown) to the end of a page or block.
Reads the body content of a page or bloc: Reads the body content of a page or block by recursively listing its child blocks, optionally rendered as markdown.
Replaces the text content of a single ex: Replaces the text content of a single existing block by id.
Deletes (archives) a single block by id,: Deletes (archives) a single block by id, removing it from its page.
Posts a new comment thread on a Notion p: Posts a new comment thread on a Notion page.
Lists all comments on a page, grouped in: Lists all comments on a page, grouped into discussion threads.
Searches the workspace by title for page: Searches the workspace by title for pages and/or databases shared with the integration, with exact or partial matching.
Lists the people and bots in the workspa: Lists the people and bots in the workspace, returning each user's id, name, and type.
Fetches a single workspace user's detail: Fetches a single workspace user's details by id.
Retrieves a Notion database's schema: it: Retrieves a Notion database's schema: its property names, field types, and select/status/relation options.
Queries a Notion database with the API's: Queries a Notion database with the API's native filter and sort JSON objects (compound AND/OR, ranges, dates, contains, etc.).
Creates a new inline Notion database und: Creates a new inline Notion database under a parent page, with a title and a property-schema object defining its columns.
Updates a Notion database's title and/or: Updates a Notion database's title and/or column schema (add, rename, retype, or remove properties) by id.
Creates a new row (page) in a Notion dat: Creates a new row (page) in a Notion database, setting its property values from a raw Notion properties object, with optional body content.
Overwrites property values on an existin: Overwrites property values on an existing Notion database row, identified by its page id, from a raw Notion properties object.
Finds rows in a Notion database matching: Finds rows in a Notion database matching a raw Notion filter object, returning the first match and all matches.
Archives (soft-deletes) a Notion databas: Archives (soft-deletes) a Notion database item by its page id, keeping it recoverable.
Restores an archived Notion database ite: Restores an archived Notion database item back to active status by its page id.
Make a custom API call to a specific end: Passez un appel API personnalisé à un point de terminaison spécifique

The id of the page to move. Resolve via: The id of the page to move. Resolve via notion_search.

The id of the page or block to append co: The id of the page or block to append content to. Resolve via notion_search (page) or notion_get_block_children (block).
The content to append. Markdown formatti: The content to append. Markdown formatting is supported. Each resulting text block is capped at 2000 characters by Notion.
The id of the page or parent block whose: The id of the page or parent block whose content to read. Resolve via notion_search (page) or this action (child block ids).

Recursively retrieve nested children up: Recursively retrieve nested children up to this depth. Only used when Markdown is disabled. Defaults to 1.
The id of the block to update. Resolve v: The id of the block to update. Resolve via notion_get_block_children.
The new plain-text content for the block: The new plain-text content for the block. Split automatically at Notion's 2000-char-per-rich-text-object cap.
The type of the block being updated — mu: The type of the block being updated — must match the block's actual type (see its type in notion_get_block_children). Defaults to paragraph.
For to_do blocks only: whether the check: For to_do blocks only: whether the checkbox is checked. Ignored for other block types.
For code blocks only: the programming la: For code blocks only: the programming language (e.g. javascript, python). Ignored for other block types.
The id of the block to delete. Resolve v: The id of the block to delete. Resolve via notion_get_block_children.
The id of the page to comment on. Resolv: The id of the page to comment on. Resolve via notion_search.
The plain-text comment to post as a new: The plain-text comment to post as a new thread on the page.
The id of the page whose comments to lis: The id of the page whose comments to list. Resolve via notion_search.
The title text (or part of it) to search: The title text (or part of it) to search for.
Restrict results to pages, databases, or: Restrict results to pages, databases, or both. Defaults to both (all).
When enabled, only return items whose ti: When enabled, only return items whose title exactly equals the query. Disable for partial matching.
How many items to return at most (betwee: How many items to return at most (between 1 and 100).
How many users to return per page (1–100: How many users to return per page (1–100). Defaults to 100.
Pagination cursor from a previous call's: Pagination cursor from a previous call's next_cursor to fetch the next page.
The id of the workspace user to retrieve: The id of the workspace user to retrieve. Resolve via notion_list_users.
The id of the database to inspect. Resol: The id of the database to inspect. Resolve a database title into its id with notion_search (filter_type=database).
The id of the database to query. Resolve: The id of the database to query. Resolve a database title into its id with notion_search (filter_type=database).
Optional. A Notion query filter object. A single condition is { "property": "Status", "status": { "equals": "Done" } }; compound is { "and": [ ...conditions ] } or { "or": [ ...conditions ] }. The condition key MUST match the property's type (e.g. status:{equals}, select:{equals}, number:{greater_than}, date:{on_or_after}, rich_text:{contains}, checkbox:{equals}). Run notion_get_database first to confirm property names and types. Omit to list all rows.
Optional. An array of Notion sort object: Optional. An array of Notion sort objects. Sort by a property: [{ "property": "Name", "direction": "ascending" }]; sort by a timestamp: [{ "timestamp": "last_edited_time", "direction": "descending" }]. direction is "ascending" or "descending".
Maximum number of rows to return (1–100): Maximum number of rows to return (1–100). Defaults to 100.
Optional pagination cursor. Pass the nex: Optional pagination cursor. Pass the next_cursor returned by a previous call to fetch the next page of results.
The id of the PAGE the new database will: The id of the PAGE the new database will live under (must be a page, not a database). Resolve it via notion_search.
The title of the new database.
A Notion property-schema object: a map o: A Notion property-schema object: a map of column name to a type-config object. Example: { "Name": { "title": {} }, "Status": { "select": { "options": [ { "name": "Open" }, { "name": "Done" } ] } }, "Estimate": { "number": { "format": "number" } } }. EXACTLY ONE property must be of type "title". Common types: title:{}, rich_text:{}, number:{format}, select:{options:[{name,color?}]}, multi_select:{options:[...]}, date:{}, checkbox:{}, url:{}, email:{}, phone_number:{}, people:{}, relation:{database_id}.
The id of the database whose schema to u: The id of the database whose schema to update. Resolve it via notion_search (filter_type=database).
Optional. A new title for the database.
Optional. A Notion property-schema patch: Optional. A Notion property-schema patch: a map of property name to a type-config object. To ADD or RETYPE a column: { "Priority": { "select": { "options": [ { "name": "High" } ] } } }. To RENAME a column, key by its current name with { "name": "New Name" }. To REMOVE a column, key by its name with the value null (DESTRUCTIVE — drops that column's data). Run notion_get_database first to see current property names and types.
The id of the database to add a row to. Resolve a database title into its id with notion_search (filter_type=database).
A Notion properties object: a map of pro: A Notion properties object: a map of property name to a typed value object matching the database schema. Example: { "Name": { "title": [ { "text": { "content": "My task" } } ] }, "Status": { "status": { "name": "In Progress" } }, "Estimate": { "number": 3 }, "Tags": { "multi_select": [ { "name": "urgent" } ] }, "Due": { "date": { "start": "2026-07-01" } } }. Run notion_get_database first to confirm property names and types.
Optional plain-text paragraph to append: Optional plain-text paragraph to append as the body of the new row (page).
The page id of the database row to updat: The page id of the database row to update. Resolve it via notion_query_database or notion_find_database_item.
A Notion properties object with the valu: A Notion properties object with the values to set: a map of property name to a typed value object. Only the properties you include are changed; others are left untouched. Example: { "Status": { "status": { "name": "Done" } }, "Estimate": { "number": 5 } }. Run notion_get_database first to confirm property names and types.
The id of the database to search. Resolv: The id of the database to search. Resolve a database title into its id with notion_search (filter_type=database).
A Notion query filter object. A single c: A Notion query filter object. A single condition is { "property": "Email", "email": { "equals": "a@b.com" } }; compound is { "and": [ ...conditions ] } or { "or": [ ...conditions ] }. The condition key MUST match the property's type (e.g. title:{equals}, rich_text:{contains}, select:{equals}, status:{equals}, number:{equals}, checkbox:{equals}, date:{equals}, multi_select:{contains}). Run notion_get_database first to confirm property names and types.
The page id of the database row to archi: The page id of the database row to archive. Resolve it via notion_query_database or notion_find_database_item.
The page id of the archived database row: The page id of the archived database row to restore. Resolve it via notion_query_database (with an archived filter) or from the response of notion_archive_database_item.
